chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The best of vegetables is the endive (hinda'), and there is no leaf of it except that upon it is a drop from Paradise. So eat it and do not shake it off when eating it. He said: And my father (peace be upon him) forbade us from shaking it when we ate it.

key_terms.الْهِنْدَبَاءُ: Endive, a type of leafy green vegetable
key_terms.قَطْرَةٌ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ: A drop from Paradise, referring to the dew on the leaves

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of eating endive (hinda') according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the medicinal and spiritual virtues of endive (hinda'), portraying it as a blessed provision where each leaf retains a drop of Paradise's dew. The specific instruction not to shake off the dew reflects the Ahl al-Bayt's emphasis on preserving the natural purity and blessings of food, a practice consistently observed by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS).

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The best of the vegetables is the endive, and there is none from a leaf except that upon it is a drop (dew) from the Paradise. So eat it and do not shake it off during eating it. My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> forbade us that we shake it when we<sup>asws</sup> ate it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The endive is a very good herb. On every one of its leaves there is a drop of paradise, so you should eat it and do not shake it off when eating.’ He (the Imam) has said, ’My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, prohibited us from shaking off when we were eating it.’”
